seo_title: Cost of Living in Ankara 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Ankara per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: The capital of Turkey in the heart of the country: visa-free entry, a business and student city without the resort markup, cheaper than Istanbul and the coast. The downsides — no sea, a continental climate with cold winters and less of a tourist scene.
pros: Cheaper than Istanbul and the coast
A business and student city without the resort markup
cons: No sea — it's an inland city
Less of an English-speaking, international scene
Not the most spectacular city in Turkey

visa_steps.title: Visa-free entry
visa_steps.description: Russian citizens don't need a visa for short trips — the stamp is issued at the border.

faq.question: Do Russians need a visa for Ankara?
faq.answer: No, no visa is needed for short trips. For long-term residence you obtain an ikamet.

faq.question: How much does it cost to live in Ankara?
faq.answer: Cheaper than Istanbul and the resorts — no tourist markup. The exact budget is in the calculator above.

faq.question: Which language is spoken in Ankara?
faq.answer: Turkish; there's less English than in tourist cities.

faq.question: Can I pay with a Russian card in Ankara?
faq.answer: No, Russian cards don't work. You need lira and a card from a foreign or Turkish bank.

faq.question: What is the climate like in Ankara?
faq.answer: Continental: hot, dry summers and a cold, sometimes snowy winter — there's no sea nearby.

faq.question: How does Ankara differ from Istanbul?
faq.answer: Ankara is cheaper, calmer and more business-oriented, but without the sea or the strait; Istanbul is larger, more spectacular and more expensive.

reviews.text: Ankara is a practical, affordable city without the resort markup, with a convenient metro and infrastructure. The downsides — no sea, cold winters and not much for tourists.
We moved for the prices and the calm: cheaper than Istanbul, less bustle. There's little English, you have to learn Turkish, but daily life is convenient and the student scene is lively.
